items.subject: 18 month survey of unsecured Ollama servers and an unsolved mystery
items.what_happened: An 18-month scan found large numbers of Ollama servers exposed to the public internet with no authentication, allowing anyone to enumerate models and run inference on them. Operators should verify Ollama is not bound to 0.0.0.0 without a network boundary and place it behind a firewall or authenticating reverse proxy.
items.why_it_matters: Classified as breaking for on-prem operators: action may be required on ollama
items.rationale: Assess exposure before the next upgrade window

items.subject: Four reproducible vLLM parser failures that return 200 with the wrong tool call
items.what_happened: Report documents four reproducible failure modes in vLLM's tool/function-call parsers where malformed or unparsed model output is returned as an HTTP 200 with an incorrect tool call instead of an error. Operators running vLLM's OpenAI-compatible server for agentic or tool-calling workloads should validate tool-call arguments downstream and check which parser their deployment uses, since failures are silent and will not surface in error rates.
items.why_it_matters: Classified as breaking for on-prem operators: action may be required on vllm, tool-calling, openai-api
items.rationale: Assess exposure before the next upgrade window

items.subject: Xiaomi AI Cube Targets Local LLMs with 1.22 TB/S Near-Memory Bandwidth
items.what_happened: Xiaomi announced the AI Cube, a compact local-inference box marketed with 1.22 TB/s near-memory bandwidth for running LLMs on-device. Memory bandwidth at this level is the main constraint on single-stream token generation, so the box is a potential small-footprint alternative to GPU servers for local model hosting, pending independent benchmarks and confirmation of supported runtimes and memory capacity.
